Concerns.Title: The East Cut
Concerns.Pitch: Come here, you'll want this one before you walk east. Bandfrogs. Three of them, nested in the east cut right where the good peat is, and every one louder than the dog. You've heard our dog, so you know what I'm telling you. Spade goes in, frog comes up. Nobody's cut out there in a fortnight, and the drying racks are as bare as a washed plate. Some years the Concord sends its pest man for thirty drams and a share of every rack after, and every year somebody says never again. Never again, never again, and then the racks are bare again.
Concerns.Thanks: Spades in the east cut again. The racks'll be full by the end of the week.

Approaches.Label: Clear the bandfrogs out of the east cut.
Approaches.Objective: Clear the bandfrogs out of Sumphold's east cut

Confront.Site: the peat cut just east of Sumphold

Approaches.Label: Pay the Concord's pest man (30 drams); he takes a share of the peat.
Approaches.OfferText: Pay the Concord's pest man: 30 drams

Refusal.Text: I won't be going out there. Better you hear it now.
Refusal.Reply: The west bank, then. Wetter peat, longer drying, and my mother beside me saying it was better in her day. It wasn't. Go on.
